recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. Further source edits would duplicate existing guidance unless the work group opens a new issue for a more prescriptive Subscription security policy.
issue_request: FHIR-18994 was Published/Persuasive for R5 and asked to add detail to Subscription security considerations, especially authorization/user privileges, payload minimization, and cases where highly specific subscription criteria can reveal PHI through the notification itself even without a payload. The Jira resolution directed the work to be handled as part of FHIR-18993.
initial_application: Commit 3a6fa70bed0cb56521fe1f91749e4e4e95f39c55 explicitly applied FHIR-18994 together with FHIR-18993 and FHIR-19621 by adding Subscription security considerations to source/subscriptions.html. Later Subscription framework edits, including fc659be95ed, reformatted/refined the section while preserving the security content in the current build.
additional_context: FHIR-18993 is the same change family and FHIR-19621 is a duplicate REST-hook HTTPS/TLS warning request addressed through that family. The active Subscription resource page links its Safety and Security section to the Subscriptions Framework safety section. The linked Zulip REST Hook payload thread aligns with the Jira/source rationale, and direct Confluence searches found no conflicting records.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source already instructs applications to authorize Subscription creation using SubscriptionTopic and filters, re-check authorization before notifications, limit payload types, avoid generating notifications that would reveal confidential information, protect sensitive Subscription data such as privileged endpoints, and validate incoming notifications while guarding against denial-of-service.

related_jiras.note: FHIR-18994's resolution explicitly says to handle the request as part of FHIR-18993, and the historical implementation commit covered both issues.
Duplicate REST-hook HTTPS/TLS security request addressed as part of FHIR-18993 and included in the same implementation commit.
